title: The V-Twin Motorcycle That Nails The Balance Between Touring Comfort And Sportbike Speed - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update The character of a V-twin engine is unmatched in the motorcycle world. Sure, a parallel-twin with a 270-degree crank has similar benefits, but the OG is still the OG. So wanting one makes total sense as an enthusiast. However, the number of V-twins has been decreasing steadily. That means finding a specialized tool can become hard if you don’t know where to look. This gets particularly worse if sport bike speed and touring comfort are your priorities, leaving you with just one Austrian motorcycle to take home. Look at the big sports bikes, and you’ll find a common way they go about producing serious power. The engines are all high-strung, compact, and rev to the moon, with most of the power concentrated above 10,000 RPM. Things are completely opposite on the V-twin side of things. More often than not, low RPM grunt takes priority here, along with large capacities rather than modern engine tech. The compression ratios are under fairly chill, too. All that means if you want sports bike-like speed from a V-twin motorcycle, you’ll be left with a handful of machines to pick from. Club touring comfort to that requirement, and you end up walking an even tighter rope. After all, all the comfort-centric V-twin tourers follow the traditional route: massive bodywork carved of steel, near-1000-pound weight figures, and understressed engines. So you will get comfort, but not sports bike speed. What do you do then? Wave the white flag and pick another engine configuration? Well, there is a solution from an Austrian brand with brilliant know-how of touring comfort and technologically advanced V-twin engines. We’re talking about KTM, which has introduced the new do-it-all 1390 Super Adventure S EVO. This is one of the most advanced adventure-tourers you can get your hands on today, so you'd better believe touring comfort and tour-centric technology are both in heaps here. At the same time, it utilizes KTM’s flagship engine: the LC8C 1,350cc V-twin. This is unlike your usual V-twins, featuring a whole lot of modern tech to produce over 170 horsepower and 100 pound-feet. If this doesn’t cut it, the next best thing is the Buell SuperTouring. It has Buell’s Rotax-derived 1190cc V-twin engine with 185 horsepower. That’s more power than the Super Adventure, but this is a more basic bike everywhere else. Oh, and orders opened not too long ago, without any official confirmation of delivery dates. Being a flagship adventure-tourer, the Super Adventure S EVO has a premium MSRP of $22,699. But that only tells half the picture. You see, the KTM undercuts all of its comparable rivals by a hefty sum. For reference, the Ducati Multistrada V4 S sells for $29,995, while the BMW R 1300 GS breaches the $28,000 mark if you want similar equipment. The $23,795 Triumph Tiger 1200 GT Explorer is the closest rival in terms of price, but it still doesn’t match the equipment of the KTM. Speaking of which, here’s a deep dive into what the KTM gets you for the price. The LC8C engine is arguably one of the USPs here. It takes the usual V-twin approach by using displacement to its advantage, but sprinkles some tech wizardry to make its case even stronger. Chief among these bits is the new Camshift technology–same as the 1390 Super Duke R Evo. This is essentially variable valve timing with two cam profiles, meaning better low-end tractability and a harder top-end punch than conventional setups. It also helps promise a mind-boggling valve check interval of over 37,000 miles. This Camshift, in tandem with larger 60 mm throttle bodies and a new 10-liter airbox (over the 1290 setup), helps produce 170 horsepower (173 PS) and 107 pound-feet. The latter trumps all of its rivals by a fair bit, and all at lower RPMs, too. It’s even 20 pound-feet higher than most flagship superbikes. In the real-world, keep it pinned long enough, and the S EVO will take you beyond 150 MPH with ease. While the VVT is impressive, the bigger headline is KTM’s AMT (automated manual transmission). A centrifugal clutch only engages as the RPMs rise, letting you roll off from (and to) a stop without using a physical lever. In the meantime, an electromechanical shift actuator works with the Transmission Control Unit (TCU) and ECU to shift gears as fast as you would with a quickshifter. Comfort, Street, and Sport modes are present to let you tweak the shift aggression, while a Manual mode gives you full control via the foot lever (a small plus considering bikes like the Africa Twin DCT have paddles). The entire package will surely help make life easier during long days in the saddle. The Super Adventure S EVO is also loaded everywhere else. You get a front radar that enables active cruise control and collision detection to make freeway riding effortless, while the six-axis IMU enables all the necessary rider aids. These comprise traction control, wheelie control, five ride modes, cornering ABS, and engine maps. You can access these via the eight-inch TFT, tucked under an adjustable windscreen. TPMS, keyless ignition, and phone connectivity are standard as well. If you’re unaware, KTM’s ‘EVO’ tag usually brings with it semi-active suspension. And that’s the case with the Super Adventure S EVO, too. Long-travel WP 48 mm USD forks and a WP monoshock are present, both offering electronic adjustment and 8.66 inches of travel. If you don’t want to adjust things, you can choose between the four semi-active suspension modes (Comfort, Street, Sport, Rain). All of these adjust the damping rates with magnetic valves in real-time to react to surfaces and rider input. You can also adjust settings via the TFT. The advanced suspension attaches to 19/17-inch alloy wheels, where the front wears 320 mm discs with Brembo monobloc calipers. A Brembo master cylinder is present, too. This should be plenty for you to shed speed fast, considering the S EVO weighs 502 pounds wet without fuel. The saddle height is tall, though, with the lowest setting being 33.34 inches. KTM’s special trellis frame with an aluminum subframe wraps things up. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. title: Odegaard and Saka star - player ratings for Arsenal v Chelsea - BBC
content: Captain Martin Odegaard scored the winner as Arsenal secured an impressive 2-1 home victory over Chelsea. Club-record £117m signing Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead after just two minutes, but Kai Havertz equalised against his former club before Odegaard struck early in the second half to seal the win. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. David Raya: The Arsenal goalkeeper was beaten by the quality of Rogers' finish but dealt comfortably with the other efforts he faced and produced one stunning save late on from Estevao. 6 Ben White: A tidy display in possession, although he made little impact at either end of the pitch. 6 Gabriel Magalhaes: Outshone by Konsa at times but still produced an effective performance. 7 Ezri Konsa: On his first Arsenal start, he won more duels than any other defender and was joint-top for possession won in the first half. 7 Riccardo Calafiori: His underlapping runs were typically adventurous and the Italy defender played a key role in creating problems from set-pieces. 7 Myles Lewis-Skelly: Fired a poor effort wide from the edge of the area late in the first half and was caught in possession in a dangerous area, but competed well in midfield. 6 Declan Rice: Played his part in a fiercely contested midfield battle and contributed well both in and out of possession. 6 Martin Odegaard: Put Arsenal ahead early in the second half with a composed finish. Also impressed with the quality of his delivery, both in open play and from set-pieces. 8 Bukayo Saka: A constant threat from set-pieces and regularly won free-kicks in dangerous positions. His impressive second-half effort was saved. 8 Kai Havertz: Passed up a shooting opportunity in the 23rd minute but made no mistake with his next chance, cutting inside to score two minutes later. Also played a part in Odegaard's goal and proved a threat at set-pieces. 7 Christos Tzolis: Delivered well from the left and provided Arsenal's main outlet whenever they broke from periods of Chelsea possession. 7 Martin Zubimendi (on 67, Myles-Skelly): A complete substitute performance involving dangerous shots, impressive passing and breaking up the play. 7 Piero Hincapie (on 67, Calafiori): Kept it simple with Arsenal ahead. 6 Mikel Merino (on 77, Odegaard): A tidy addition late on in midfield. 6 Viktor Gyokores (on 78, Havertz): Not much opportunity to make an impact as Arsenal held onto their lead. 5 Emiliano Martinez: There was concern when the Argentina goalkeeper was accidentally kicked in the head by Gabriel early on, but he was beaten too easily at his near post for Havertz's equaliser. He later made a high-quality save from Saka in the second half. 5 Josh Acheampong: Often dragged into uncomfortable areas by Tzolis from a tactical perspective, but handled his individual defensive duties well. 6 Maxence Lacroix: Miscontrolled a ball early on and allowed Havertz's shot to pass through his legs but also impressed at other times. 6 Wesley Fofana: Unconvincing defensively against Saka, Odegaard and, ultimately, Havertz for the equaliser, but the most composed of Chelsea's defenders in possession. 6 Pedro Neto: Tasked with marking Calafiori while also providing an attacking threat. Hit the post just before half-time with a brilliant curling effort. 7 Reece James: Saw a well-struck long-range effort saved after 22 minutes and was arguably Chelsea's best passer. 7 Romeo Lavia: Produced a superb defensive header to clear the danger in the 32nd minute and competed aggressively throughout. 6 Jorrel Hato: His determination helped create Rogers' volley and he matched that effort defensively, although he struggled to contain Saka at times. 6 Cole Palmer: Had one effort on target in the first half and was booked for a professional foul. Also had a second-half shot saved. Arsenal largely kept him quiet. 5 Morgan Rogers: Opened the scoring with a first-time volley after just two minutes. Later curled an effort narrowly wide in the 31st minute and was Chelsea's most dangerous attacking player. 7 Joao Pedro: Unconvincing defensively at set-pieces and had few opportunities in front of goal, including an ambitious effort from distance. Still made a significant contribution through his work-rate, physical presence and ability to bring team-mates into play as the number nine. 6 Malo Gusto (on 60, Lavia): Poor effort moments after coming on, albeit playing out of position in central midfield. 5 Pep Chavarria (on 60, Hato): Struggled to track his runners on a few occasions. 6 Estevao Willian (on 80, Neto): The Brazilian's sensational curling effort almost levelled but was saved by Raya. Subs not used: Penders, Colwill, Barco, Quenda, Gittens After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. title: Opinion | Norway's Harald V forged strong ties with U.S. - The Capital Times
content: Hannah Rosenthal: We must renew the fight as we watch the ga… Peggy Wirtz-Olsen: Wisconsin voters should research politica… Norway Ambassador Tom Loftus (left) and King Harald V (right) attend the opening of the United States exhibit at the annual offshore oil industry trade show in Stavanger, Norway, in 1996. The man in the center is an aide to the king. The passing of King Harald V on Aug. 28 was a sad day for Norway. His son now King Haakon VIII will take the throne. During my time as the United States ambassador to the Kingdom of Norway, from 1993 to 1998, I was with His Majesty many times. My very first official act was to present my credentials as the representative of President Bill Clinton. It was in the palace, and when the door to the reception room opened the king was standing and smiling. A great smile that had brought creases to the tanned cheeks of the former Olympic sailor. When we parted the king said, “We will see each other often.” Most notable was when I escorted him and Queen Sonja on their first state visit to the United States. It started with me dancing with the queen at the welcoming reception at the Waldorf Astoria in New York, and ended with a state dinner in the private dining room of President Clinton and First Lady Hillary Clinton. On April 9, 1940, Hitler’s Nazi Germany launched a surprise invasion of neutral Norway. The goal was control of the fjords for German submarines and to capture the king and the crown prince so they could not form a government in exile. They escaped to London. The Crown Princess Martha and the three children, two girls and a 6-year-old boy name Harald, left Oslo in a motorcade fleeing to neutral Sweden. Sweden was not safe, and President Franklin Roosevelt sent a Navy ship to an arctic seaport to bring them to America, where they stayed in the White House. FDR helped Harald with his homework and took him fishing on the presidential yacht. He is the boy seen standing behind FDR in the photos of the fourth inauguration. At the state dinner, the king recounted his memories. This was the beginning of the modern bond between Norway and America. Norway was a founding member of NATO, and because it was the only member bordering the Soviet Union, it became essential to the Alliance. More than 800,000 Norwegians immigrated to America, one-third of the population at the time. A large number came to Wisconsin, including my grandfather, Edward, who left Norway with his parents and siblings on July 4, 1885. The descendants of these immigrants have special ties to Norway that perhaps surprisingly have strengthened over time. The passing of the king will be memorialized by the Sons of Norway among many other groups. My last official act before leaving Norway was to pay my respects to His Majesty. His parting words were, “How fast this time has gone.” I was awarded by His Majesty the Royal Order of Merit Cross of St. Olav for “outstanding service in the interests of Norway.” In my memoir, "Mission to Oslo," I recount in detail the dozen or so times I was with King Harald. Ambassador Tom Loftus is the author of the award-winning memoir "Mission to Oslo: Dancing with the Queen, Dealmaking with the Russians, Shaping history." title: Takeaways from Arsenal's 'deserved' win v. Chelsea - Yahoo Sports
content: Joe Prince-Wright shares his thoughts pitchside at the Emirates following Arsenal's 2-1 win over Chelsea to maintain their undefeated start to the season. Full-time here at the Emirates Stadium, and it finished Arsenal two, Chelsea one. Some of the analysis and reaction from being here on site, I think Kai Havertz really changed this game for Arsenal. His positioning in that first half drifted out to the right. That's how he scored that equalizer at a really important time for the Gunners, and that set the tone for the rest of the game. Chelsea had chances in the second half in particular, on the counterattack, set pieces, but they just could never find that composure in the final third. When it came down to it, when it mattered most, they just seemed to rush those chances. The fans and the players was a little bit nervy towards the end of the game. I think, as I wrote about it, on three things we learned over on Pro Soccer Talk at NBCSports.com, that this rivalry is back. For a long time now, Arsenal have dominated Chelsea in so many ways. But today, with Alonso's appointment, the fact that Chelsea have closed that gap to Arsenal, it feels like a considerable amount this summer and will continue to do that, it does feel like Chelsea are back, and this rivalry is gonna be back, for the next few years in the Premier League. There was a little bit of a wry smile when Alonso and Arteta, the old friends, embraced at the end of this game. Of course, a great game, great spectacle, but Arsenal did get the deserved win. In terms of some of the other things I, I like the look of, in t- I, I just think Chelsea did a great job from set pieces. No Premier League team, so far this season has scored more set-piece goals than them. And Austin McBeath was out, directing all of, the corners, the free kicks. Did a really good job of just those small margins, and Chelsea looked a lot more dangerous, going forward, with these, set-piece opportunities. Then defensively as well, the fact that they left four players up really bamboozled Arsenal a little bit. Arsenal had to leave more players back, and they weren't as big of a threat, from those set-piece situations when Chelsea put four players up. The Arsenal fans singing to him, "You should have signed for a big club." And I think, again, the fact that the rivalry is back, if you look at him and Declan Rice, England teammates, get on well, but it was pretty feisty at the end as they squared up when Rice caught Rogers there in a bit of a, a nasty, flick off the ball. Arsenal one, they've won three straight games, to start the Premier League season. As for Chelsea, I think they underlined to everyone here they can just tweak a few things defensively, if they can get a bit more composure, in the key moments up front, then I think they're gonna be the main contenders, along with Man City, for the title this season. For Arsenal, I feel there's still just that bracket under- underneath them, Chelsea, but certainly was a positive performance for Xabi Alonso's side for a lot of this. And yeah, Arsenal I think will go away thinking, "Okay, we've got another contender here that we have to fight with this season for the title." And like I said, Havertz was excellent, degaard was excellent, and overall some really good, intriguing individual displays in terms of positioning on the pitch. And in terms of the atmosphere, the rivalry, how feisty it was here inside the stadium, loved it, and this is a big London derby, and it's great to have it back, in this kind of form. So head over to Pro Soccer Talk on NBCSports.com for all the latest from here in North London. Going down to the tunnel area now to speak to the players from both teams, so keep an eye on that. First big, big game of this Premier League season in terms of a battle between the big boys. Arsenal came out on top, but Chelsea showed they're improving and they're catching up.

title: Everton v Man Utd player ratings: Jack Grealish returns but which sub made the biggest impact? - BBC
content: Benjamin Sesko scored after coming off the bench with 20 minutes remaining Ainsley Maitland-Niles crashed home a thunderous long-range shot as Everton scored in stoppage time to earn a 2-2 draw at home to Manchester United. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. Maitland-Niles stunner earns Everton point against Man Utd Jordan Pickford: Not the busiest afternoon for the England keeper - might have done better for the goal. 6 Merlin Rohl (off 74, Hackney): Encouraged to get forward more by team-mates but seemed wary of leaving too much space behind him. Did provide the cross that Thierno Barry should have headed in. 6 James Tarkowski: Long ball straight to Senne Lammens in the second half drew groans from the crowd and a stream of invective from his manager. 6 Jarrad Branthwaite: Strong defensive performance, not afraid to get his body in the way of Man Utd shots and a brilliant tackle on Rashford. Found time to have a go at goal himself at the other end. 8 Vitalii Mykolenko: Found himself in space to create something inside the Man Utd box but failed to make the most of the opportunity. Got behind Bryan Mbeumo at the start of the second but again the outcome was poor. 6 Harrison Armstrong: Cautioned for needlessly dragging Bruno Fernandes round the neck, but a minor blot on an otherwise impressive performance. Easy to see why the Everton fans reacted so fiercely to the prospect of him being sold. 7 James Garner (off 76, Maitland-Niles): Decent effort against his old club. Worked tirelessly in defence and going forward. 7 Brennan Johnson (off 66, Grealish): Picked ahead of Jack Grealish but not the greatest game going forward. Blatant foul on Matheus Cunha earned a booking but probably worth it as it stopped the Brazilian racing into the box. 6 Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: Industrious performance in the middle of the pitch went unrewarded in terms of result but would have been appreciated by boss David Moyes. 7 Tyrique George: Started well and lifted the ball over Mbeumo with superb skill. Drifted out of the game in the second half, until he beat Lammens. 6 Thierno Barry: Lucky not to be booked for a clear dive early on to try and win a penalty. Headed Everton's best first-half opportunity over from close range. Overhit a pass that could have sent Johnson through. 5 Jack Grealish (on 66): Ran at Diogo Dalot and drew a yellow card from the Man Utd man. Clearly determined to make an impact. His presence roused Everton's fans for a big finish. Tied Mbeumo in knots as he tried to set up an equaliser. 7 Hayden Hackney (on 75): Played the pass for the equaliser. 6 Ainsley Maitland-Niles (on 77): The decisive contribution. 8 Subs not used: Mark Travers, Michael Keane, Jake O'Brien, Tyler Dibling, Charly Alcaraz, Braiden Graham. Senne Lammens: Made a mess of a routine ball into the box, although he had been impeded by Dewsbury-Hall. Aside from that, usual unflappable self. Saved the shots you would expect. 6 Diogo Dalot (off 84, Yoro): Another fortunate to escape an early yellow card for hauling back Tyrique George. Solid after that though and strong in the tackle. 6 Harry Maguire: Needed treatment for a bloody nose in the opening minutes but recovered and produced usual calm display. Partnership with Lisandro Martinez very effective. 6 Lisandro Martinez: Excellent effort from the Argentina defender. Positioning superb and didn't dive in for rash challenges. Got in the way of a Johnson shot as Everton pressed for an equaliser. 8 Luke Shaw (off 91, Mazraoui): Excellent effort and his fitness is so crucial now for Michael Carrick. Good block to stop an Armstrong effort and nipped in as Johnson was about to shoot. 8 Kobbie Mainoo (off 84, Santos): The usual smooth display, taking the ball and moving it on. Precise cross-field pass to Mbeumo led to the opener. 7 Youri Tielemans: Long-range effort didn't cause Pickford any problems. Went about his business quietly but still to see a stand-out performance. 6 Bryan Mbeumo: Quiet first half when a lot of his best work was in defence. Brilliant goal at the start of the second though. 8 Bruno Fernandes: Volleyed against the bar from a Mbuemo nod back, had another first-half effort deflected over and another blocked. 7 Marcus Rashford (off 70, Dorgu): Another eye-catching performance from the England man. Cunha wasted some of his excellent approach work. 8 Matheus Cunha (off 70, Sesko): Started in the number nine position and tried to exert influence but wasted an excellent chance midway through the first half. 6 Patrick Dorgu (on 70): Game went crazy after he came on. 6 Benjamin Sesko (on 70): Thought he had scored the winner here for the second season running. Needs to stay fit. 8 Subs not used: Karl Darlow, Mason Mount, Joshua Zirkzee, Ayden Heaven. title: The Next Kia Sportage Looks Tough Enough To Bully The CR-V Into Submission - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update The CarBuzz spy team has spotted the upcoming new Kia Sportage and this time it's doing something we don't think owners will ever do. The test mule is in Spain where the sun is still hot, and it is towing a trailer for durability testing. We've spotted the new Sportage a few times before, and so the basics aren't much different. The new Sportage will trade the curvy look of the one on sale now for a shape that's much more angular and much more upright. The chill vibe of the current SUV will be gone, replaced by a K4-like model that looks like it punches holes in doors on the weekend. Why is Kia making such a big change? The Korean brand always makes big changes, but this? It seems to bring the Sportage more inline with the Telluride, but really it goes well beyond its bigger sibling in terms of boxiness. Hyundai, with the new Tucson and Santa Fe, is going in the same direction. It's a strange convergence of the brands. Back to the trailer. We can't tell quite how heavy the rig behind this Sportage is, but it clearly has some mass. The rear end of the Sportage is slammed to the ground, with the tops of the rear tires disappearing into the arches. In the US, the current Kia Sportage has a tow rating of 2,500 pounds if the trailer has its own brakes. In Europe, that maximum is much higher at around 3,600 pounds. This Sportage appears to be at that second limit, and it might need to have some weight moved around to ease up on the trailer tongue. You can expect Kia to lean into hybrid electrification with the new Sportage. The group's new two-motor hybrid system is almost guaranteed. The system launched with a 2.5-liter turbo-four in the Hyundai Telluride, but a 1.6-liter engine version is coming. That's the one you'll find here, and the group says the system delivers 45% better fuel economy than gas alone. The Sportage has offered a plug-in hybrid system for years, and this one probably will too. Our spies have hinted that it will deliver more range, with closer to 60 miles on the WLTP cycle than the 34 miles EPA estimate of the current model. The compact crossover market remains hot, but it is also seeing a shakeup. The RAV4 is set to fall out of the top spot for the first time in more than 10 years because of a lack of supply, and that leaves the door open for competitors. With Hyundai Group's new Pleos infotainment and improved fuel economy, the Sportage is going to be a hot ticket. The question, then, is if the new styling will win buyers or push them away. It looks strange to us so far, but the brand has a strong track record of successful designs. The full reveal of the all-new Sportage should happen in mid-2027, with the SUV on sale at dealers not long after. Which is probably not soon enough to capitalize on Toyota's stumble. title: Spencer V. Kilby Obituary Aug 29, 2026 - The Asheville Citizen Times

May 15, 1998 — Aug 29, 2026 Posted online on September 6, 2026 Spencer Vaughn Kilby entered heaven’s gates surrounded by family on August 29, 2026, after an almost four-year battle with cancer. Though he fought hard, this battle did not define him. He was a warrior in every sense of the word, refusing to back down and choosing joy through it all. He was an avid Tar Heel and Manchester City fan, loved listening to music and playing video games with friends. Spencer was a chess player and a history buff, always learning new things—but most of all, he was a family man. He adored being a father, husband, son, brother, and uncle. His faith in the Lord was the reason behind why he lived the way he did and why he loved so fiercely. He was born in Asheville, North Carolina, on May 15, 1998, and was preceded in death by his paternal grandparents, Reverend Roy and Wanda Kilby, and his maternal grandparents, Wade Reece and Katrina Cobb. He later grew up in Ada, Oklahoma, where he graduated from Ada High School. Spencer and his family then moved to Houston, Texas, to receive the best care possible. He was well-traveled, but home was wherever his family was. He is survived by his loving wife of five years, Rachel Kilby, and his five-year-old son, Roan Kilby; his parents, Penny Brown (Jason) and Ryan Kilby (Jessica); his two brothers, Paxton Kilby (Sadie) and Chandler Kilby (Caroline); his step-siblings, Jackson and Ethan Boles, Dylan (Ciara), Corey and Taylor Brown; his grandparents, Vickie Reece and Earl Cobb; his seven nieces and nephews, Jamison, Kobe, Malia, Joshua, Wade, Zade, and Erin; his aunts and uncles, Pat Kilby (Angela), Lee Kilby (Anne), April Long (Tommy); and many wonderful cousins. title: William V. Finn Jr. - Oswego County Today
content: William V. Finn Jr., 88, a resident of Oswego passed away at his home on September 3, 2026, surrounded by his loved ones. Born in Brooklyn, N.Y., He was the son of the late William V. and Helen (Barry) Finn Sr. He received his Bachelor’s degree from the State University of Oswego and his Master’s degree in Education from Syracuse University.  He started his teaching career as a Special Education Teacher and retired as the Head of the Reading Department.  William retired after 34 years having spent his entire career with the APW School District.  Due to his love of Teaching he then worked at the National Grid Energy Center as a Tour Guide at their Edcation Center. William was a veteran of the United States Army, serving in the early 1960’s.  He was also a proud Member of the New York State Teacher’s Association.  He had several hobbies and interests including completing the daily crossword puzzle (in pen), golfing and woodworking.  He would spend hours in his shed making things for his family and friends. One of his biggest loves was caring for the numerous Dogs he had over the years.  He could always be seen in his neighborhood walking his Dog multiple times per day.  William enjoyed spending time with Family and Friends, especially his monthly Lunch Date with close friends.  A Special Thank You to Bill Reidy and Sam Amedio for helping make sure he made it to the lunch AND their home visits. William was also know for his sense of humor, always starting a conversation with a joke.  The highlight of each year was his Christmas Gift exchange with his Sister-in-Law, Kay Bradshaw.  They would exchange gag gifts for years with each trying to 1-up the other. Surviving are his wife of 64 years, the former Sally Donovan, and four sons: William (Tonya) Finn of Newark and Gary (Laurie) Finn of Oswego. Robert Finn of Oswego, Daniel Finn of California, four grandchildren: Emily Finn, Katie Finn, Eric Finn and David Finn. The family will receive friends on Wednesday from 1:00- 3:00 at the Dowdle Funeral Home with a service to follow. title: Sutton's predictions: Arsenal v Chelsea - Yahoo Sports
content: Arsenal were a bit clunky last time out against Aston Villa, while I love what Xabi Alonso is doing at Chelsea. He doesn't care about possession, and that's not how Chelsea try to get results. It's strange because I had a look at how his Bayer Leverkusen side lined up when they won the Bundesliga, and they were pretty dominant possession-wise. So, it is quite alarming when you look at the two league games Chelsea have played and see how much of the ball they haven't had. Against Fulham they only had 38% possession and then against Brighton it was down to 25%. I don't know whether that is by design or by just not having the players to dominate. They are still free-scoring, but they are conceding loads of goals too. Whatever the reason, I don't see it changing here. Arsenal are so powerful and the only question mark around them is if they are a forward or two short. Even so, you would not exactly say they have a real weakness anywhere. The beauty of Mikel Arteta's side is they can play in different ways. They demolished Manchester City in the Community Shield with some pure football, and played some nice stuff against Coventry too, but then they were able to grind out a win at Aston Villa as well. Ultimately, whether they are free-flowing or not, their organisation should see them through this game too.

title: Arsenal v Chelsea Match Preview: Huge London Derby at the Emirates - Yahoo Sports
content: Arsenal return to Emirates Stadium on Sunday looking to make it three Premier League wins from three when Chelsea arrive for a huge London derby. Mikel Arteta's side followed their opening victory with a 1-0 win away at Aston Villa, while Chelsea have also collected maximum points after beating Fulham and Brighton. With both teams perfect so far, something has to give at the Emirates. Xabi Alonso has settled quickly after taking over at Chelsea, winning his opening two league matches and also recording a League Cup victory. The Blues beat Fulham before edging Brighton 4-3, with their attack already looking dangerous. Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro have combined impressively in the opening weeks, while Chelsea's attacking wing-backs have also given them another threat going forward. However, the amount of change within their squad may give Arsenal something to exploit. Chelsea have already conceded five goals in their opening two Premier League matches and have looked vulnerable from balls into the box and set pieces. The contrast between the two sides defensively has been significant so far. Arsenal have faced just 11 shots across their opening two Premier League matches, with only one hitting the target. Their opponents have generated just 0.54 xG. That defensive control could be crucial against a Chelsea team that have scored seven league goals already. Arteta is certainly wary of their attacking threat. Speaking ahead of the match, he pointed to Chelsea's ability to score early and change the momentum of games, while also acknowledging Alonso's ability to set his team up in different ways. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League meetings with Chelsea, winning six and drawing three. The Blues have also lost their last four league visits to the Emirates by an aggregate score of 11-2, with their last victory here coming in August 2021. Arsenal's wider London derby record is equally impressive, with just one defeat in their last 29 Premier League games against teams from the capital. Bukayo Saka will also be looking to continue his strong start after scoring in each of his opening two Premier League appearances. Both clubs arrive with confidence, both have six points, and Chelsea clearly possess enough attacking quality to cause problems. But Arsenal's recent dominance in this fixture and their defensive solidity should give Arteta's men every reason to believe they can maintain their perfect start.
